This was primarily due to a $7.9 million deterioration on discontinued business, partially offset by improvements on other lines and strong investment income. Additionally, the syndicate noted a slight deterioration in the total expected loss for Coronavirus-related claims and poor experience in the Space market affecting 2022 policies. Inflation was a key focus for the Directors, impacting reserve strength.

gpt-5-mini.standardized_narrative: The syndicate opened 2023 with gross claims outstanding of 341.747 million (presentational currency USD). During 2023 the Managing Agent reports an overall deterioration on closed years (2014-2021) of $1.3m, driven primarily by adverse development on discontinued business partially offset by improvements on other lines and strong investment income. No single prior-year catastrophe is quantified as driving this movement; reserve movements by LOB are not explicitly broken down. The syndicate also reports several 2023 and prior catastrophe scenarios and modelled RDS/AEP losses (e.g. Katrina/Maria, Gulf of Mexico windstorm, AEP scenarios) and a notable individual 2023 Energy loss at the Nohoch (Cantarell) platform.

gpt-5-mini.data_quality_notes: Amounts are reported in the syndicate's presentational currency (USD) as used in the report. Opening gross claims outstanding taken from the Technical Provisions reconciliation (Claims outstanding balance at 1 January). Prior-year development amount taken from Managing Agent narrative stating an 'overall deterioration of $1.3m for the closed years' (closed years defined as 2014-2021). No explicit 'Movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding' table line was located; LOB-specific prior-year reserve breakdowns were not provided, so lob_movements is empty. Some named event losses are modelled RDS/AEP estimates (shown in the report) rather than actual paid net losses; confidence scores reflect clarity/quantification in the report.
